title: Introduce tenant cooldown window and progressive egress-trimper to reduce cascade during KV pressure spikes
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background: During a recent incident we observed KV pressure propagation causing regional latency amplification that then triggered broad circuit opens and customer-visible errors. This PR adds a short-lived tenant cooldown window combined with a progressive egress-trimper so tenants that suddenly produce heavy inter-region KV pressure are slowed gracefully instead of causing hard failovers.

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds a tenant-level cooldown timer (default 30s) that gates rapid burst admission, an egress-trim algorithm that reduces outgoing shard/egress rate proportionally with a decaying tenant credit, and a KV-pressure probe that feeds the cooldown trigger. The approach aims for graceful degradation: reduce egress and allow KV caches/replication to stabilize rather than tripping global circuits.

Design notes and motivation: The core idea is to break the feedback loop between KV pressure and aggressive failover. Instead of immediately escalating to regional failover or wide circuit opens, we: 1) mark offending tenant cohorts as 'cooldown' with a short TTL, 2) apply a progressive egress cap that reduces per-tenant egress by 10%-to-80% over the cooldown window using an exponential decay, and 3) surface telemetry and tracing for cooldown events so operators can observe causes. The cooldown is ephemeral and will auto-lift once KV pressure metrics recover or the TTL expires.

Behavioral rules and safety: - Cooldown TTL is configurable via runtime flags and feature gate (defaults: 30s TTL, initial trim 25%, max trim 75%). - Cooldown is tenant-cohort-scoped (not per-route) to avoid over-enforcement and preserve critical low-volume routes. - The egress-trim algorithm preserves fairness by weighting reduction by recent token usage and SLA tier. - Telemetry emits a cooldown_event with tenant_id, reason (kv_pressure|egress_overrun|manual), applied_trim_pct, and trace_id for runbook correlation.

Implementation summary: - runtime/adm/tenant_cooldown.{cc,h}: new cooldown store with TTL and probe integration. - runtime/egress/trimmer.go: progressive-trimmer implementation with an interface used by admission controller. - controlplane/flags.yaml: new flags and feature gate definitions. - telemetry/events.go: cooldown_event shape and exporter hooks. - tests/*: unit + integration harness that simulates KV pressure bursts and asserts that circuits are not opened during temporary overloads.

Rollout plan: - Feature-gate disabled by default. Stage rollout to canary region for 24h (QA & perf canaries) -> staged 10% of tenants via sampling -> 50% -> global. During canary we monitor cooldown_event rate, KV pressure, and token latency quantiles.

Rollback plan: Disable feature gate or set max_trim_pct=0 to effectively no-op. All changes are guarded behind the runtime flag so rollback is fast.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for trimmer edge cases - [x] Integration test with KV pressure harness - [x] Telemetry emitted and validated in test sink - [x] Documentation in ops-runbook (short note) - [x] Feature flag and runtime defaults added

Related tickets: Linear ENG-8792, ENG-8801. Incident reference: #INC-2026-0210-KV-SPILL.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the admission path concurrency, the lock-free cooldown cache implementation, and the fairness weights in the trimmer. The trimmer intentionally avoids hard rejects — it only reduces egress allowance so higher-SLA tenants still make forward progress albeit slower.

Operational runbook snippet (single-line style for copy/paste): "To disable cooldown quickly: POST /admin/runtime/flags set feature.tenant_cooldown=false; or set trimmer.max_trim_pct=0."

release_notes:
- Add tenant cooldown window (configurable TTL) to reduce KV-pressure-driven cascades.
- Introduce progressive egress-trimmer to gracefully throttle tenants during short-lived overloads.
- Emit cooldown_event telemetry for observability and runbook correlation.
